newsitem.title: USA: Emerging markets debt mixed, spreads narrower.
newsitem.headline: Emerging markets debt mixed, spreads narrower.

text.p: Emerging markets debt traded narrowly mixed on Thursday, with Brazil bonds outperforming other Bradys and spreads over Treasuries generally narrower, market experts said.
"It's fairly quiet, with just a little profit-taking," said a trader at a large U.S. investment bank. "We've seen strong buying in Brazil."

In late-afternoon trading, Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were up 1/2 at 79-1/8 bid, boosted by success of a re-election amendment and the country's anouncement on Wednesday that it will swap or buy back some of its Brady debt, traders said.
Brazil's Senate on Wednesday approved a bill to allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and certain other government officials to run for re-election.
Earlier on Wednesday, the country said it would either repurchase par bonds and discount Z-L bonds or swap pars, discounts or "C" bonds for 30-year uncollateralized global bonds.
Both developments helped Brazil spreads narrow sharply over the past two days, trader said. "I think there were also some locals unwinding short positions today," one trader said.
While Brazil's performance buoyed the rest of the region on Wednesday, it detracted on Thursday, some traders said.
"Basically we're getting a reallocation from Argentina and some of the exotics into Brazil," one trader said.
Other major Latins were unchanged to lower. Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR were unchanged at 93 bid, and Mexico Pars MX625L19=RR were off 1/4 at 74-7/8.
Ecuador spreads suffered from investor concern over the upcoming referendum on President Fabian Alarcon's mandate, traders said.
"There was a little bit of profit-taking in Ecuador given the referendum this weekend," one trader said.
Ecuador Pars ECPARS=RR were down 1/4 at 44-5/8 bid.

Elsewhere, Poland Discounts POFLTO24=RR were up 1/8 at 98 bid, dollar-denominated Russian Vnesh loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were off 3/8 at 85-5/8 and Phillippines Pars PH425L18=RR were unchanged at 87-1/8 bid.
U.S. trading is expected to end at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT on Friday, and there will be no trading Monday in observance of the Memorial Day holiday.
